chunks: Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari said: I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far the Second (peace be upon him),
when a man asked him, saying: 'Inform me about the Lord, Blessed and Exalted — He has Names and Attributes in His Book, and are His Names and His Attributes the same as Him?'

So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'This speech has two aspects. If you are saying they are Him, meaning He has number and multiplicity, then Exalted is Allah above that. And if you are saying that these Attributes and Names have eternally existed, then "eternally existed" carries two meanings. If you say they have existed eternally in His Presence, in His Knowledge, and He is deserving of them, then yes. But if you are saying that their images, their spellings, and their letters have eternally existed, then we seek refuge with Allah that there would be anything with Him other than Him.'

'Rather, Allah was and there was no creation, then He created them as a means between Him and His creation — they beseech Him through them and worship Him, and they are His Remembrance. And Allah was and there was no Remembrance, and the One Remembered through the Remembrance is Allah, the Eternal who never ceases to be. And the Names and the Attributes are created things, and the Meaning and the One Meant by them is Allah, upon Whom neither variance nor combination befits, for only what is fragmented varies and combines.'

'So Allah is not said to be combined, nor Allah little nor much, but He is the Eternal in His Essence, for whatever is besides the One is a fragment, and Allah is One, not fragmented, and not imaginable through fewness or manyness. And everything that is fragmented or imaginable through fewness or manyness is a creation evidencing its Creator. So your saying "Allah is All-Powerful" informs that nothing frustrates Him, and you negate powerlessness through that word, making powerlessness to be other than Him. Similarly, your saying "Knower" negates ignorance through the word. And when Allah annihilates things, He annihilates the image, the spelling, and the syllables, and He who never ceases to be remains ever a Knower.'

Then the man said: 'How then did we name our Lord All-Hearing?' He said: 'Because nothing of what is perceived through ears is hidden from Him, and we do not describe Him with the hearing situated in the head. Likewise we named Him All-Seeing, because nothing of what is perceived by vision — colour, person, or otherwise — is hidden from Him, and we do not describe Him with the glance of the eye. And likewise we named Him Subtle, due to His Knowledge of subtle things, such as the mosquito and what is more concealed than that.'

— the place of its growth, its intellect, its desire for mating, its tenderness toward its offspring, its watching over one another, and its transference of food and drink to its children in the mountains, wildernesses, valleys, and wastelands. So we know that its Creator is Subtle without a modality, for modality belongs to the created thing that has modality. And likewise we named our Lord Strong — not with the strength of violence known from creatures. For if His strength were the strength of violence known from creatures, resemblance would occur, and increase would be admitted; and whatever admits increase admits decrease; and whatever was deficient was not eternal; and whatever was not eternal was powerless.

So our Lord, Blessed and Exalted, has no resemblance, no opposite, no equal, no modality, no limit, and cannot be envisaged by sight. And it is forbidden to hearts to form His likeness, to imaginations to limit Him, and to consciences to conceive Him. Majestic and Mighty is He above the instruments of His creation and the features of His created beings, and Exalted is He above that, a Great Exaltation.

key_terms.أَسْمَاءٌ وَصِفَاتٌ: Names and Attributes — the divine names (al-asma al-husna) and qualities attributed to God in the Quran
key_terms.الْقَدِيمُ: The Eternal/Ancient — a divine attribute meaning God has no beginning and is uncaused
key_terms.تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى: Blessed and Exalted — standard honorific for God
key_terms.مَخْلُوقَاتٌ: Created things — in this context, the formal expressions of the Names are created, not the realities they point to
key_terms.مُتَجَزِّئٌ: Fragmented/divisible — the Imam's key criterion: everything that can be divided or multiplied is created

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia Islamic understanding of God's Names and Attributes according to Imam al-Jawad?
ai.summary: In this profound theological discourse, the ninth Imam Muhammad al-Jawad (AS) responds to a question about the relationship between God's Names and Attributes and God Himself. The Imam explains that divine Names and Attributes should not be understood as co-eternal with God in their formal or linguistic expression, for that would imply multiplicity in the divine essence; rather, they are created means through which creation relates to God. The Imam then elucidates God's transcendence by showing that divine attributes like All-Hearing, All-Seeing, Subtle, and Strong negate their opposites (deafness, blindness, coarseness, weakness) from God rather than ascribing creaturely properties to Him — a sophisticated apophatic theology rooted in Shia Imami tradition.
